classification.difficultyReason: Apply the median-position rule in both directions to complete a paired table.

inlines.text: Copy and complete the following table, which relates the number of data values to the position of the median. (A position of 5.5 means that the median is the average of the 5th and 6th data values.)

answer.worked:
For $n$ ordered values, the median position is $p=\dfrac{n+1}{2}$; a half-integer position means averaging the two adjacent values.

$$\begin{align*}p_{11}&=\frac{11+1}{2}=6\\p_{21}&=\frac{21+1}{2}=11\\p_{20}&=\frac{20+1}{2}=10.5\\p_{100}&=\frac{100+1}{2}=50.5\end{align*}$$

For a given position $p$, there are $p-1$ values on either side when $p$ is an integer; equivalently, $n=2p-1$. The same rule gives the even number of values for half-integer positions.

$$\begin{align*}n_{15}&=2\times15-1=29\\n_{22}&=2\times22-1=43\\n_{13.5}&=2\times13.5-1=26\\n_{24.5}&=2\times24.5-1=48\end{align*}$$
